title: Page fragmentation + bank interleaving: microburst latency investigation
content:
Summary:

This is a working log for an investigation into small (10-200ms) tail-latency microbursts observed on multi-tenant inference hosts. Symptoms are transient token-level latency spikes correlated with ephemeral decreases in KV cache reuse and bursts of DRAM/PCIe activity. Hypothesis: page fragmentation combined with suboptimal physical bank interleaving (on machines with 4-channel DDR + NUMA) amplifies memory channel contention during KV spillback and prefetch windows, causing microbursts.

Why this matters:
- Microbursts translate to token-level latency jitter for latency-sensitive customers (chat/streaming).
- Existing batch/eviction heuristics assume stable BW; fragmentation introduces nonlinearity (small increases in working set -> large BW spike).
- Can degrade SLOs even when avg throughput and occupancy look fine.

What we observed (high level):
- Repro runs where a background synthetic workload (mix of short 8-64 tokens and long 2048 tokens) runs alongside a pinned model instance show occasional 30-120ms tail spikes affecting short requests.
- When host memory is highly fragmented (after repeated warmups + allocations), we see larger instantaneous DRAM read bandwidth and increased PCIe NVME spill reads.
- Perf counters show sudden increase in LLC miss rate and memory controller queue length coincident with the latency spikes.

Hardware / Software baseline for tests:
- HW: 4x A100 hosts, 2-socket CPU (dual-socket E5/Cascade style), 4 memory channels per socket, interleaved physical mapping. Tests primarily on internal dev box with similar topology.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15 (we also retested on 6.1 for one run).
- Serving: local dev build of serving-runtime (commit referenced in linked_artifacts PR).
- Model: reference GPT-like 7B variant used in KV stress harness.
- KV subsystem: current prod allocator (buddy), default page size (4KB), no explicit page coloring.

Reproduction recipe (quick):
1) Start baseline cluster with two tenant groups: heavy long-seq (L) and high-throughput short-seq (S).
2) Warm L group until KV resident set ~80% (run repeated context warmups to fragment page allocations).
3) Inject spike load: a 10s burst of mixed S requests every 60s.
4) Capture perf and host telemetry: perf stat -e LLC-load-misses,mem_load_uops_retired.l3_miss -I 1000; nvidia-smi dmon for GPU stats; collect /proc/vmstat and /proc/pid/io.

Commands used for detailed captures (examples):
- perf record -a -g -o perf.data -- sleep 60 (followed by perf script stack collapse)
- perf stat -e cycles,cache-misses,LLC-load-misses,mem_load_uops_retired.l3_miss -I 1000 -p <pid>
- sudo cat /proc/vmstat > vmstat_snapshot.txt (before/after spike)
- iostat -x 1 60; sar -r 1 60
- lscpu and numactl --hardware to check interleaving; /sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo

Key measurements (representative run):
- Baseline avg request p95 without fragmentation: 22ms.
- During fragmentation-run microburst: p99 increases to 210ms for short requests (observed 12 spikes in a 10min run).
- LLC misses during spikes: +3.6x relative to baseline window.
- Measured DRAM read bandwidth instantaneous peaks: ~1.9x sustained above long-run mean for ~30-150ms windows.
- NVMe read IO throughput for spillback: increase of 2x, small increase in read latencies to 10-15ms per IO (single SSD).

What we changed and effects:
1) Aligning page allocations to prefer page-coloring-like contiguous bank spread (user-space allocator tweak to use libnuma to allocate with interleave=all)
   - Result: spikes dropped in frequency by ~40% but not eliminated. Peak BW still hits but less often.
2) Use hugepages (2MB) for KV structures and pre-touch on allocate
   - Result: reduces LLC miss amplification; p99 improves ~15% and spike frequency reduced further. Hugepages reduced page fragmentation at the cost of slightly higher reserved memory.
3) Forced NUMA binding of long-seq tenant to single socket, short-seq tenants affinitized to other socket
   - Result: isolating sockets reduced cross-socket memory storms but introduced uneven GPU/CPU affinity and scheduling complications.
4) Kernel vm.swappiness -> 10, vm.dirty_ratio tweak to reduce async writeback pressure
   - Result: small improvement in NVMe write bursts but not primary cause.

Telemetry traces (notes):
- Time-aligned traces show LLC miss spike -> DRAM bw spike -> NVMe spill reads (in some runs) -> request latency spike. Path suggests that when a set of pages are scattered across banks, the effective memory controller cannot coalesce reads and causes increased queueing latency and slower prefetcher effectiveness.

Hypotheses refined:
- Page fragmentation causes multi-page working sets to map heavily to the same memory channels temporarily (bad interleaving), producing local bank saturation and amplified read latency for the affected pages. Because KV prefetched entries are touched in microbursts, the memory controller queue amplifies the contention in sub-100ms windows.
- Hardware interleaving patterns + kernel allocator behavior under repeated allocate/free cycles create periods of pathological locality.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much of this is specific to our platform's chipset memory interleaving algorithm vs. general across cloud instances? Need tests on AMD EPYC and other cloud instance types.
- Is there a safe, low-cost allocator change (user-space) that will avoid bank skew without forcing hugepages? Page-coloring emulation or simple stride-aware allocator?
- Impact on memory footprint and fragmentation long-term if we switch to hugepages for KV: what is the tradeoff for multi-tenant hosts?

Short-term mitigations to try in staging:
- Prefetch smoothing: throttle KV prefetch rate in presence of rising llc-miss BW (done inside runtime; immediate quick experiment).
- Staggered warmup: warm large models in phased steps to avoid large simultaneous page touches.
- Enable optional hugepages for only the largest KV tables (config flag).
- Add runtime telemetry for "instantaneous BW pulse" detection (short moving-window BW estimate) and fall back to conservative eviction / prefetch thresholds.

Longer-term ideas:
- Implement a bank-aware page allocator shim in user-space runtime that attempts to spread large contiguous KV allocations across banks by querying /sys or using libnuma hints.
- Collaborate with infra to run a matrix across CPU types (Intel X, AMD EPYC, cloud VM types) and kernels to identify platform-level failure modes.
- Explore page coloring via kernel patches or use of hugetlbfs with partial-hugepage management.

Experiment matrix (planned):
- Factor A: Kernel (5.15, 6.1, 6.4)
- Factor B: Page size (4KB, 2MB hugepages)
- Factor C: Allocation strategy (buddy default, numa interleave, custom allocator)
- Factor D: Synthetic workload mix (S-only, L-only, S+L mixed with 1:4/1:8 ratios)
- Factor E: Host types (intel-x, amd-epyc, cloud-x-large)

Next steps / action items:
- [Aisha] Complete controlled matrix runs for two kernel versions and collect p99/p999 latency, LLC misses, DRAM BW (ETA 2024-12-12).
- [Marcus] Prototype a lightweight allocator wrapper that uses numa_alloc_onnode / interleave hints and measure fragmentation after 1h of churn (ETA 2025-01-05).
- [Omar] Run cross-platform smoke tests on two cloud instance types (GCP n2-standard + azure vmX) to validate platform dependency (ETA 2024-12-22).
- [Team] Decide if we roll hugepage option to staging by 2025-01-15 if results are positive.

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Could leverage a cheap latency detector: moving-window standard deviation of token latencies; on detection, temporarily reduce prefetch aggressiveness and increase TTL for cached entries to avoid immediate re-touching spilled pages.
- Consider combining prefetch smoothing + eviction hysteresis so hotset is kept compact and page touches spread.

References and related tickets:
- JIRA-INFR-4512 (investigation ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/839 (allocator shim prototype)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-RT-7622 (notes and planned experiment grid)

Appendix: raw snippet from perf window where spike occurs (example):
- timestamp 12:13:10.342: LLC-load-misses +34523 -> mem_bw instantaneous 48 GB/s -> p50-> p99 jump
- /proc/vmstat around spike: pgfaults +240, pgmajfaults 0, pswpin 0, pswpout 0 (indicates not swapping but heavy reads)

End of notes - this is a working document, expect iterations.
